summary.en: Choose storage at run time and follow its lifetime from allocation through release.
summary.bn: রান টাইমে মেমরি নাও আর কখন সেই মেমরি ছাড়তে হবে তা বুঝে কাজ করো।

notes: These complete programs target C17; declarations in loops require C99 or later.

sections.title: A room you rent while the program runs
Habits to use in your programs

examples.title: One allocated mark
examples.explanationHtml: The allocated integer receives 78 before printf reads it. main then releases the block.

examples.title: Allocate room for three marks
examples.explanationHtml: The marks 60, 65, and 70 give a total of 195.

examples.title: A helper returns a live allocation
examples.explanationHtml: make_mark transfers ownership to main; its allocated integer outlives the helper call.

practice.title: Store lab marks at run time
practice.statementHtml: Read count from 0 to 20, followed by count marks from 0 to 100. Print Count and marks: on its own line, then their total. For count zero print 0 without allocating.
hints: Keep the allocation until all input has been checked.

practice.title: Fill a requested block
practice.statementHtml: Read count from 1 to 20 and value from -100 to 100. Print Count and value: then the first and last initialized elements, separated by one space.
hints: Every element must be written before it is read.

practice.title: Return an allocated result
practice.statementHtml: Read a mark from 0 to 100. Print Mark: then the same mark obtained from a helper that returns an allocated int. The caller releases the result.
hints: Allocation lifetime continues after the helper returns.

practice.title: Reverse owned values
practice.statementHtml: Read count from 1 to 20, then count integers from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then the integers in reverse order, separated by spaces. Use dynamic storage and release it.
hints: Count down from count and access index i-1.

quiz.prompt: Which lifetime does malloc create for its successful result?
quiz.explanation: The caller controls the allocation lifetime through free.

quiz.prompt: Where are malloc and free declared?
quiz.explanation: The allocation functions are declared by stdlib.h.

quiz.prompt: What does a local int * retain about an allocated array?
quiz.explanation: Keep array length separately; a pointer value carries no length.

quiz.prompt: Why is *mark assigned before printing in the first allocation program?
quiz.explanation: Reading an uninitialized allocated int has no usable value guarantee.
options: malloc does not initialize the integer

quiz.prompt: Which pointer may be passed to free while its allocation is live?
quiz.explanation: free requires the allocation base or NULL, with the lifetime still active.
options: An address of a local int

quiz.prompt: Does returning from make_mark automatically release its allocated integer?
quiz.explanation: The local pointer ends, but allocated storage follows a separate lifetime.
options: Yes, all storage ends on return
Only if the mark is zero
No, the caller must arrange release

quiz.prompt: How should an empty dynamic collection be represented without a zero-byte request?
quiz.explanation: A NULL owner with zero length clearly describes an empty collection.
options: A dangling pointer and one count
A local int address passed to free

quiz.prompt: Which single stored mark is printed before the block is released?
quiz.explanation: The assignment sets the allocated integer to 78.

quiz.prompt: What total is accumulated from the three allocated marks?
quiz.explanation: The loop stores and sums 60, 65, and 70.

quiz.prompt: Which mark survives the make_mark helper return?
quiz.explanation: The allocated object remains alive until main releases it.

keyPoints.en: A dynamic block can outlive the helper that allocated it.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যালোকেশন করা ব্লক হেল্পার ফাংশন শেষ হওয়ার পরও থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Keep the element count beside an allocated array pointer.
keyPoints.bn: ডাইনামিক অ্যারের পয়েন্টারের সঙ্গে এলিমেন্টের সংখ্যাও রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Check allocation before accessing its target.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যালোকেশন সফল হয়েছে কি না দেখে তারপর মেমরি ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: malloc storage needs initialization before value reads.
keyPoints.bn: malloc দিয়ে পাওয়া মেমরিতে পড়ার আগে মান বসাও।

keyPoints.en: The owner releases the allocation once its work ends.
keyPoints.bn: কাজ শেষ হলে মালিক পয়েন্টার ধরে মেমরি একবার ছেড়ে দাও।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish automatic and allocated storage duration using a returned int pointer.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A local int ends when its block ends, so returning its address leaves a dangling pointer. An allocated int lasts until it is released. Returning its base address can transfer ownership to the caller.

examQuestions.question: Explain the separate lifetimes in int *p=malloc(sizeof *p), including failure and release.
examQuestions.answerHtml: p is a local pointer. If malloc returns NULL, there is no owned integer to access. Otherwise the allocated integer must be initialized before reading. free(p) ends that allocation; p itself still exists but must not be used as a live target. Assigning NULL gives p an empty state.

Returned mark: 85

The helper initializes 85; main prints it before calling free.
